definition: A popup is a visually separable message surface that is not part of the primary screen scaffold, navigation, or inline host content and that visibly overlays, occludes, gates, or interrupts the current host context.
visual_separability_rule: At least one screenshot-observable cue must distinguish the message surface from host content: a bounded container or edge, a different apparent z-layer or backdrop treatment, host-content occlusion, or a full-screen gate/interruption composition. Temporal persistence and inferred dismissibility are never required.

edge_rules.bottom_sheet: popup only when visually separable and interruptive or gating; otherwise no_popup or uncertain
edge_rules.full_screen_surface: popup only when the screen presents a distinct gate or interruption rather than the stable primary page
edge_rules.banner: popup only when it is a persistent blocking or gating message surface; transient toast/snackbar is excluded
edge_rules.consent_notice: in scope when it is an ordinary non-permission notice or choice; OS-level and app-internal permission or security controls are both out of scope in V1
edge_rules.permission_boundary: all OS-level permission dialogs and all app-internal permission or security controls are out_of_scope in V1, even when they are visually paradigmatic popups; this is a study-boundary decision, not a claim that they are unimportant
edge_rules.actionability: do not infer dismissibility, clickability, or available actions beyond explicitly visible labels

include_visible: explicitly visible choice labels needed to understand the message
message_definition.critical_fact_rule: A visible fact is critical only if omitting or changing it could materially alter understanding of the message; retain negation, amount, date/time, object, condition, restriction, and explicit consequence.
